Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **kagex-release encrypts and hides names on Windows, whatever language the file names are in**: a game with a file named in Japanese, built on an English Windows, stopped with "No mapping for the Unicode character exists in the target multi-byte code page" ([xp3crypt](https://github.com/krkren/xp3crypt) 08ad5f7 takes names through UTF-8)
- **Archives with hidden names match names without regard to case**, as plain archives do: `title.PNG` loaded as `title.png` failed with "Unknown graphic format". The 0.9.4 engines have the fixed plugin
- **A game's own `startup.tjs` runs in a build with hidden names**: it goes into `data.xp3` as `startup-game.tjs`, and 0.9.4's `hashed-bootstrap.tjs` runs it once the archives are mounted. Update a game's `data/system/hashed-bootstrap.tjs` from `template/system`; with an older one kagex-release warns that `startup.tjs` won't run
- **kagex-release's `--engines` can be relative to the current folder** (an unpacked engine package failed in the Windows icon and version step)
- kagex-release 0.9.4 downloads the 0.9.4 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.9.4/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
